Did Mr. Thebault report to you around this time, as reflected in the early part of the document and at the last paragraph, that he had had some contacts with this General Praljak in connection with the presence of HV troops or support in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: Now, I have no prior knowledge of this document. It appears to be a genuine ECMM document, but as you will see, it is dated 30 July, which is after I left the mission. It refers to the special report of 3rd of June, and the reporting here is consistent with what had been reported on the 3rd of June, and it is consistent with the ECMM assessment of the situation. But I have had no knowledge of this report until it was shown to me here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Let me ask you a separate question, then. Were you aware, at the Zagreb level of ECMM, whether in fact various senior HV officers -- generals, commanding officers -- had moved across and taken very senior positions in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: As a general statement, yes, I believe that to be true and correct. But I have no, shall we say, concrete recollection of names and times and dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Let's move forward, then, to 943,2. I apologise for the quality of the copy, but it seems to be the best available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: On mine, my bundle, you're going back.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The number -- Your Honour, maybe we could substitute. It may be the bundle, unfortunately, has not been prepared as well as it might have been, and we could substitute additional -- a different bundle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It is true that some of the exhibit numbers do drop back down, but, as I indicated at the outset, in that sense some of the documents are out of order. But the order should have been correct in the bundle itself. Looking at 943,2. I just want to direct your attention to about a third of the way down the page. It talks about the foreign minister, Niels Helveg Petersen. Do you see that? Have you found that? With reference to that, did it come to your attention there was a meeting or series of meetings about the conflict in Central Bosnia, in Medjugorje, on about the 18th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: Yes, we were aware of this meeting. Of course, it was with the participation of the Danish minister for foreign affairs, Helveg Petersen. I did not participate myself, because we thought it was better for Mr. Thebault, who had the detailed knowledge from the ground, to represent the ECMM there; especially since both the co-chairman would be there, Lord Owen, and Mr. Vance. So we would not need to be involved at the, as you say, the policy level. That would be taken care of by the minister and the two co-chairman, but we thought it would be helpful if they could rely also on information provided by the ECMM.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Did you understand that among the other participants in these meetings were President Izebegovic from Bosnia-Herzegovina, President Tudjman from Croatia, and Mate Boban?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: Yes, that was known to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you provide any assistance to the Court in terms of why it was that President Tudjman was involved in this meeting concerning a resolution of the conflict in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: It was the assessment of the ECMM that Croatia, and of course President Tudjman, had a large degree of influence on what happened on the site of the Bosnian Croats. So in that respect it would be natural to see to it that President Tudjman would be present.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you relate to the Court a particular event around that time where a senior Danish official, perhaps the foreign minister, had had some direct conversation with Mr. Tudjman, President Tudjman, about these matters?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: As appears from this document, it was Mr. Helveg Petersen, the foreign minister, who himself made the statement, and explained to President Tudjman, as it was said in the document here, that he should use his influence with the Bosnian Croats to bring hostilities to an end. Now, for the information of the Court, perhaps just the information here, that this is not an ECMM document. This is a document coming from Minister of Foreign Affairs in Copenhagen. So, in effect, this represents the summary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the meeting in Medjugorje. It is not the ECMM's summary of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well. In fact, this was the one document in the list earlier today that you'd identified as different, somewhat distinct from the other documents listed in the Exhibit Z2788?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: That is true. This is a document sent from the presidency to the other capitals of the European Union with information on the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Before moving on in that same general part of the document, it states: "It was clear, from President Tudjman's own statement and his general demeanour, that he felt put under heavy pressure and that he recognised that he himself had to use his influence with the Bosnian Croats to bring hostilities to an end." Again, this was a part that was being reported not to just your government but to all the EC governments at the time?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: It was not reported to my government. This is my government's report to the other governments of the European Union.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Let's go on to Exhibit -- Your Honour, these are the three now -- the next three are the ones that were separate from the bundle, that I introduced, were offered, tendered this morning. The first one is 939,1, which they were distributed earlier. With reference to about the middle of that page -- not really the middle of the page; about a third of the way down the document it refers to a "General Cuk of the HV also present." This document is about the same series of meetings at Medjugorje on 18th of May; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. President, one point in connection with this document. It appears to be incomplete, since there is a reference to an Annex 1, approximately halfway down the page, and I don't have an Annex 1 on my document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We don't, Your Honour. This is the only part that we have at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No doubt efforts can be found to find the annex.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Only one question about that, sir. Do you have any reason why this HV General was participating in these meetings, either you or -- if not yourself personally, ECMM?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: Well, this meeting took place in Medjugorje on 18 May, when the meeting with the foreign minister and the co-chairman took place, and President Tudjman, so it would be entirely consistent that President Tudjman would come not alone but with a number of his staff present.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Going on to Exhibit 910,1, which again is one of the loose exhibits, if you will. 910,1. Can you describe for the Court what that document is, or actually series of documents?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: The cover note is in Danish. Would you wish me to give a translation of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: "This is sent to the minister of foreign affairs by the political adviser, Christian Warming." And it states that, "ECMM has, for the possible use of the EU presidency, prepared a draft to President Tudjman. And for the information of the ministry, enclosed is also a copy of President Tudjman's statements concerning the situation in Central Bosnia." And point 2: "... the approval of the ministry, the ECMM will hand over the enclosed protest to Mate Boban."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: For the record, can you say, what is a demarche?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: Demarche is a diplomatic term for a meeting in which you voice the concern, the opinion of your government, or the institution you represent, vis-à-vis the interlocutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Would you then go on --

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: It is normally considered a term that you would only use for, shall we say, most solemn occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could you go on to the second page of that document and tell the Court what that is.

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: This is a PM, which is diplomatic slang for pro memoria. That is a piece of paper that you would hand over to the person you are talking to, which would summarise the message you are conveying on behalf of your government or of your institution. So this will normally not be the full text of what is actually being said to the person you are talking to, but it will be a short and concise summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: This one was in particular being directed by the European Union to the President of Croatia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Among other things, President Tudjman is being called upon to exercise all his influence with the Croat leadership of Herceg-Bosnia; that it brings an immediate end to the HVO aggression in Central Bosnia, especially in Mostar; that the blatant violations of humanitarian law is stopped. And the last item: "Further, the President of Croatia is called upon to withdraw all HV military personnel and equipment from Bosnia-Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: This statement, of course, is based on our assessment of the situation on the ground. It is not in our hands, the ECMM, to decide the final fate of this PM. To be honest, I have no clear recollection of how this was transmitted to President Tudjman, and by whom. I am confident it was not transmitted by the ECMM. It could have been the co-chairman. It could have been the Danish Ambassador to Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: At what level would such a document normally be communicated to a head of state?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: It would always be communicated at the level of head of mission, which in most cases will be ambassador, or in some cases Charge d'Affaires.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you look to the next page and just tell us what that appears to be?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: That is an excerpt from HINA, which is a Croatian press agency.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is that a government press agency or is that an independent press? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: It is an independent agency, but of course operating within the laws of Croatia at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And we won't go through the document in detail. This is some response, apparently, made by President Tudjman in connection with these documents that were faxed to you by Christian Warming on the 11th of May. What's finally the third or, excuse me, the last document, "Dear Mr. Boban." Can you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: That is a draft letter to Mr. Boban to be signed by the head of mission of the ECMM, Mr. Skor, Ambassador Skor, which is referred to in the cover note, that we were seeking the ministry's approval before transmitting it to Mate Boban.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, whether the document like this was in fact finally transmitted to Mr. Boban?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: I am confident that it was, but I would hesitate to state it with certainty. I believe it was, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well. And the next one is Exhibit 937,1, which is the last of the so-called loose exhibits. Mr. Warming was a political adviser that worked with you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Only one highlight on this document. Next to the final paragraph on page 2, the paragraph that begins with the words "Mate Boban," but a little over halfway through that paragraph, is this statement, and I'll simply ask again if this is consistent or was in fact an ECMM assessment. "To all intents and purposes, much of Herceg-Bosnia was, by late 1992, behaving as an integral part of Croatia, and in practice the Bosnian Croats, Croatian Council of Defence, HVO, continue to resist any joint command with the Bosnian armed forces loyal to the Sarajevo presidency." Was that ECMM's view?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: It was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: With reference, then, to Exhibit 963, which should be again back in the bundle, Exhibit Z963. Looking at the number -- item number 3. Only this question, and perhaps you know separate from the document. The meeting that was held in Medjugorje on the 18th of May, 1993, do you know whether it was in fact President Tudjman who had initiated that meeting?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: I have no clear recollection of who called the meeting. I assume that it was President Tudjman, since it is written here, but I have no clear memory as to exactly what took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: There are several possible explanations. It could have been at the suggestion of the co-chairman that he call the meeting; it could have been at the suggestion of the presidents in Copenhagen. So the fact that he hosted the meeting does not in itself mean that he was the one who took the initiative to have it arranged.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: As I said, I have no recollection of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let's move on to Exhibit Z993. This is a bit different than the other documents, the ECMM documents we've seen so far. Can you tell the Court what document this is?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: This is a series of documents prepared for the morning briefings. At the morning briefings in Zagreb we would normally expect the chief of operations, or one of his assistants, to give a fairly detailed account on the events in the last 24 hours. But it was always introduced as sometime during our presidency, I don't remember exactly when, that we should have also reports of a more in-depth nature so as to give a better perspective to the mission leadership, but also to the monitors, on what was going on, because these briefings would be communicated to all the teams.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And again just a couple of highlights on what would be the fourth page of the document, including the cover page. A couple of paragraphs up from the bottom of the page. It was again reflected that: "It was the clear conviction of the EC, or European Community, that Croatia, which was de facto deeply involved, had to play a prominent role for the clear acceptance of the peace plan by the Bosnian Croats and their respect for democratic principles."

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: That was our assessment at the time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If the Court will allow me, this is again one of those documents which has an extreme amount of relevant information, but for the purposes of this witness and time, we won't go through it in any greater detail. If we can continue on, then, to Exhibit 937, which is a -- it starts with a cover page and then a report on the situation in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, we'll let that document, for the time being, speak for itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The reference to Exhibit Z1008,1, did it come to your attention, sir, that around the 1st of June, 1993, two Danish civilian drivers in a convoy had been killed in Bosnia in connection with their being involved in a humanitarian convoy?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: Yes, it did come to our attention. They were not ECMM drivers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, not ECMM, but they were Danish drivers, and around the same time, there had been some Italian, I believe, some Italian drivers that were killed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: From the ECMM's position, was it increasingly difficult during this time to assist in getting humanitarian aid into Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: It was difficult all through our presidency, but it became increasingly difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I can go on to Exhibit 1013, I will just advise --

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: Would you allow me to go back to the document here?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Certainly. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: It being presented in this case here would tend to support a thesis that there was one particular party which was behind the -- the incident at Maglaj. I think I owe it to the Court to say that it is my opinion or assessment, based on information other than this document, that there is no clear evidence that the Bosnian Croats were involved in this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well. But in terms of in general, you had indicated earlier that it was the ECMM's assessment there was an HVO policy of restricting movement in Central Bosnia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And simply the overall state of affairs continued to make it more and more difficult to get aid to various locations in Central Bosnia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Let's go ahead, then, to Exhibit 1013.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And I'll just point out, Mr. President, and to the Defence, that there is an identical document in a different format that follows immediately on, for whatever reason, printed out in different -- again, different format. But it's somewhat easier to read than the other version.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: This is a special report from the head of RC Zenica dated the 3rd of June, 1993, covering a number of matters, but for the present purposes, let me direct your attention, please, to the last paragraph on page 2, meaning -- well, the last paragraph on page 2, if you are using the clearer version of the document. Was it Mr. Thebault's report at that time, and ECMM's assessment, that the third problem, this third problem, was "more worrying. It concerns the presence of real Bosnian Croats extremists in the provincial authorities, like Messieurs Valenta or Kordic, both HVO vice-presidents at the national level in province Travnik. They will be, de facto, the real powerful people in the provincial authorities, and using the absolute majority the Bosnian Croats have due to the absence of Serb representatives, they will be able to use and abuse the fact that most of the decisions will be taken with simple majority." Was that the assessment, sir?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: It was Mr. Thebault's assessment, and shared by ECMM headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: This had to do with the establishment of provisional provincial governments under the Vance-Owen Plan; is that what is being discussed here?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm only going to touch on 1053,1 to simply indicate that again, this is a report from Mr. Thebault dated the 13th of June, 1993, and we will leave it for the time being to speak for itself, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Going to Exhibit 1064,1, can you tell us the circumstances surrounding this -- sending this communication to Mr. Boban?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: To my recollection, we had a report from the field that the three interpreters and the driver, they had been taken hostage by HVO soldiers. We discussed in Zagreb what to do. It is my recollection that apart from sending this letter to Mr. Boban, a similar protest was sent by UNPROFOR and UNHCR -- could be UNPROFOR or could be in the name of the U.N. military observers; I'm not quite certain. My recollection is that it was a concerted action to secure the release of the people taken hostage.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell the Court whether the HVO did subsequently release these individuals?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: They were released. I'm not certain about the time frame, but it was sort of close in time to the letter here. Whether it happened immediately or a day or two after, I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Going on to Exhibit 1061, this is a document, appears to be, that you were a little bit more directly involved in yourself; is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Just tell the Court the circumstances surrounding this document.

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: I had been invited by Mr. Ganic, the vice-president of the BH government, to come to Geneva in order to take place meetings with the co-chairmen. It so happened that the meeting did not really take place as foreseen, but it gave us the opportunity to hold meetings with Lord Owen and with Mr. Ganic. I was accompanied, as you will see from the report, by Mr. Bees, who was the deputy head of RC Zenica, a very competent man, and he and I had the talks mentioned in the memo and in subsequent documents. We were -- after the meeting with Lord Owen, during the meeting, we were asked by Lord Owen to prepare a briefing paper for him; he was going off to see the German government. And since we brought the newest information from the field, he was grateful that we would prepare this paper for him. The extent to which it was used, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Directing your attention, then, to the briefing paper itself, which is, including the cover page of the document, would be the fourth page, titled "Croat/Muslim Relations in Central Bosnia," is that a copy of the paper that you and Mr. Bees prepared?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Down that page, was it the assessment at the time of the HVO aims that they appear to be, "(a), militarily establish a front line between provinces 8/10 and the 'Moslem' 9; (b), eliminate all Moslem resistance to their plans within provinces 8 and 10; (c), eventually cleanse provinces 8 and 10 of Moslems in pursuit of their dream of 'Herceg-Bosna'; and (d), establish a loose confederation with Croatia in due course." Was that ECMM's assessment of HVO's aims or objectives in June of 1993?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: That was our assessment, and the more so that we would be very careful with the wording in the document to be given to Lord Owen for the purposes stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: This document, then, you're saying, was not lightly prepared?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: No, it was not. In terms of language in the paper, you will perhaps see that it is not the normal strict, dry language of a foreign-office memo. This was because it was prepared for Lord Owen, for his own eyes, to use for the briefings. So it was not brought into a more terse format, exactly because we wanted also to give the atmosphere or the assessment of the situation, and that was based on -- in this kind of language.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Before continuing on, then, on the next page, under heading 5, "Action required to reduce tension," sub-item (c), did the ECMM continue to push, and was it your recommendation to Lord Owen that Croatia continue to be pressured or influenced in some way to "terminate HV military activity and all other material support for the HVO in Bosnia-Herzegovina, such as troops, weapons, and money"?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: It was our assessment, at the time, that there was still HV involvement inside Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I think also that with the circumstances of preparing this document for Lord Owen going to see the German chancellor, it would be natural for us to make a special point of highlighting the assessment that there was still HV involvement and supplies.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And if we can then continue on to Exhibit Z1065. Again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, looking at the clock --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- we must try and finish this witness by -- at least in chief -- this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I fully intend to, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Is the witness able to come back tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's not too inconvenient? Very well; thank you. As far as the other documents are concerned, you may be able to take them a little more briefly --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- if you just refer us to the relevant passages.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Z1065 is, again, a particularly substantial document. The rest of the documents from then on, which are only -- I don't know, perhaps four or five -- we can simply basically identify. But I do have every intention to be completed by 1.00, if not sooner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, just to complete what Judge May just said, it's not necessary for all these documents to be read by the witness. If you attract our attention on the relevance of this and this, and having the document identified, in particular when we have gone before to the same subjects, like to the Vance-Owen Plan, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I will do the rest quite quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: With reference to 1065, sir, again, this appears on its face to be a document in which again you were more extensively personally involved; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court again the circumstances for preparing this particular document?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: We were coming towards the end of the Danish presidency. We had not achieved exactly what we came there to achieve, namely peace. So I think this was sort of my valedictory dispatch to the presidency, and to the co-chairmen and whoever cared to read it, our assessment of the situation. It is written under my name, but of course it was based on the combined efforts of the mission. Christian Warming was involved in writing it, and not least Charles McLeod. So based on reports from the field, based on the work of the three of us, this is how it ended. And this, I think, is our best attempt at a fair assessment of the situation towards the end of our presidency, and with recommendations for whatever action could and should be taken by the western governments in order that things may be speeded up. It still took a couple of years before it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Just as a matter of historical interest, is it your view that in fact the recommendations made here were largely many of the actions which were ultimately taken to end the war?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: I think that's fair to say. However, I wouldn't think it's based on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: But as I said, this was not my personal opinion only. It does represent my personal opinion, but it was a combined effort at the mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me direct your attention, then, to only one paragraph of this long document, paragraph 16 on page 4, talking about command and control of the HVO. I don't think it's probably necessary to read out loud the entire paragraph, but if everyone could have the paragraph in mind. You state here, sir, at the end of that paragraph, "In the Novi Travnik/Vitez/Busovaca area, HVO preventing the movement of relief convoys answer only to Dario Kordic, minister for Herceg-Bosna in the HVO government, political leader, effective military commander in Busovaca, and cousin of Mate Boban." I do see, in passing, moving on, that I will make a quick reference to paragraph 22 on page 5, and the document also goes on to talk about such things as the Convoy of Joy and about Croatia's relationship. Paragraph 22, stating about -- a little over halfway through the paragraph, "A loss of political support from Croatia could pressure the HVO into accepting a ceasefire." The ECMM's assessment, sir, throughout your six-month tenure, or the term of the presidency, continued to be -- I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Just in the interests of completeness, Your Honour, I think that the full sentence on page 22 should be read into the record, and not half of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Happy to. "A loss of political support from Croatia could pressure the HVO into accepting a ceasefire or serve to incite them to pursue their objectives in isolation, becoming more defiant and desperate."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I was saying before, was it your assessment -- when I say "your," ECMM's assessment -- throughout the six months of the presidency of Denmark that in fact there was this strong connection between the government in Zagreb and the Bosnian Croats?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me just simply point out that -- if you look at Exhibits 1079 and 1079,2, which are the next two exhibits, reports by Mr. Thebault dated the 19th of June, 1993. Mr. Brix Andersen, if you'll have those in mind, and the Court have those in mind, and you can simply keep a finger there. And if you go on to Exhibit Z1086, which is another ECMM report. Exhibit Z1086, at page -- well, if you use the stamp numbers on the top of the page, the last two digits would be 23. Starting with "RC Zenica." Is it correct, as you explained throughout the course of this morning, sir, that the reports that would come up from the field, if you will, would often then be incorporated into other reports that would then be passed on from the headquarters level; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: Yes. The team reports would be coming up through the system, but the team reports would also, according to a system we devised early on in our presidency, the team reports would also become available in full to the headquarters, so we could make excerpts of whatever material we thought was relevant, and to send it off unedited to Copenhagen for their use.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And the only point being there is that it illustrates the point, Your Honours, that the Court can see on the part of 1086 that I've directed your attention to, starting with "RC Zenica," that that report then goes on for the next couple of pages to essentially restate or incorporate, if you will, the two individual reports from Mr. Thebault. The content is basically either the same or very, very close. Referencing only one paragraph in 1079,1, and then finally after that, Your Honour, going to the last document. I simply point out the third paragraph starting on the second page of 1079,1. And Mr. Thebault reports, states: "It seems machiavellic, but it is only Balkan. And everyone who has met regularly the top Bosnian Croat leaders, Messrs. Boban, Stojic, Kordic, Valenta, in various situations and on various subjects, where their paranoia and extremism were not hidden, can easily believe it. " In reference to this memo, sir, did ECMM also come to know that -- were there instances in Central Bosnia where the Bosnian Croats moved, if you will, some of their own population in order to attempt to arrive at certain goals?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: As appears from the reports, on the evidence here, it was our assessment, certainly the assessment of the people on the ground, that some of the movements were not because of direct, imminent threats from the Bosnian government forces, but it was largely at the instigation and under the control of the Bosnian Croats themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In fact, if the Court will allow me one final reference in this document. The paragraph immediately preceding the one we mentioned before, cites an example or the rationale for just such movements. If you see that, sir. "... need to reinforce Croat populations in certain areas."

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Finally, if you can go to Exhibit 1149,1. A further report dated the 22nd of July, 1993, from Mr. Thebault; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: Yes. After I had left Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. But in terms of the first two paragraphs on the first page, under the title of the memo, is it correct, sir, that the reports and observations made by Mr. Thebault were consistent with the ECMM's assessment during the previous six months?

utterances.speaker: OLE BRIX ANDERSEN
utterances.text: Yes, they are consistent, although, as I said, it's after my departure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, I don't know what the value is of having this witness produce documents which he did not originate but were originated by another witness we may be hearing from.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: For several reasons. Well, if I may, Your Honour. For several reasons. One is what he has said, what the witness has said throughout the morning, is that these were not just the positions, for instance, of RC Zenica or Mr. Thebault, but represented the institutional assessment of ECMM and, at the very highest levels, many of which were communicated to a number of European and union governments. And I think that additional level that he can add to the documents, albeit as one step removed from the ground, is true. But again, as the deputy head of mission, we thought that it was important for him to put these documents in that particular context. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Is there anything else in chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That concludes the evidence in chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That concludes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Cross-examination, I hope, will be completed by tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Absolutely no question that the cross-examination will be completed by tomorrow, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You'll leave enough time for Mr. Kovacic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Most certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Brix Andersen, I'm afraid we haven't finished your evidence today and we are not in a position to sit this afternoon. Could you be back, please, tomorrow at half past 9.00, when I trust your evidence will be concluded. Could I remind you, as I have to remind every witness, not to speak to anybody about your evidence until it's over, and that does include members of the Prosecution team.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you would like to go now, please be back tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let me return the documents, which were the additional documents I was given. Give them back to the Prosecution, please, with thanks. Mr. Sayers, if I was to say that an order to the Registry has been signed to take place immediately, does that deal with the matter you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: If I can intuit the content of the order, I would suspect it does, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If there is any difficulty about it, would you report it this afternoon to the legal officer?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Immediately, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Tomorrow morning, half past 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: 12.58 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 1st day of December, 1999, at 9.30 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
